⊢.justification: Before any problem instance or witness exists, the computational universe is void — no verifier, no certificate, no reduction

≻.justification: Forward morphism maps any NP problem instance to a SAT instance via Cook-Levin, directed toward the verification target

≺.justification: Contravariant morphism descends from the verification boundary into the exponential witness space, reversing the reduction direction

⋈.justification: Sequential chaining of witness bits through the verifier's transition function, composing local checks into global acceptance

⊙.justification: The verifier recognizes its own transition function; the horn torus pinch ⊙ is the geometric self-reference where μ∘δ = id

∈.justification: Splits into accepting arm (witness validates) and rejecting arm (witness fails) — the fundamental decision of the verifier

∋.justification: Rejoins accept/reject arms into the single verdict register; conflicting witnesses fuse to B (both) at the critical boundary

⊤.justification: Constructive truth: a witness exists that makes the verifier accept in polynomial time

⊥.justification: Constructive falsity: all witnesses are rejected; the verifier finds no accepting path

⊞.justification: At the critical threshold ⊙, the verifier simultaneously holds accepting and rejecting configurations — the B state where P vs NP becomes a live contradiction

⊡.justification: Each verification step writes an append-only record; the (16,3) knot winding fixes the computational history permanently
